summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, abdominal pain, and back pain, concerning for pyelonephritis and acute on chronic kidney injury, with a creatinine of 7.2. Imaging and a loopogram revealed a left ureteral obstruction causing severe hydronephrosis. A left percutaneous nephrostomy was placed for drainage, leading to improvement in renal function. Urine cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterococcus, prompting a switch from meropenem to gentamicin. He completed a two-week course of IV antibiotics via a PICC line, which was removed prior to discharge. A nephroureteral stent was placed to maintain drainage, and the patient was transitioned to oral pain medications. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for urology follow-up and stent exchange in three months.
